_comment: A locked-down kiosk: one application, fullscreen, no way to leave it.
Read README.md next to this file before deploying it. Three of the
settings below are load-bearing and one of them is dangerous.
The keys marked _DANGER_ are commented out. Turn them on deliberately,
and only once you have another way into the machine.
_url: The shell. Absolute path, because the compositor resolves it as a URL
and not against the working directory. Point it at wherever this
checkout lives, or at an installed copy.
_startup: The application. This is the only thing the compositor launches, and it
is launched exactly once — nothing restarts it if it exits.
That is deliberate: a restart loop belongs to something that can back
off, log, and give up, which is a service manager and not a compositor.
In production make this a systemd user unit with Restart=always and put
the unit name here. The shell shows 'waiting for it to come back' while
no window exists, so a supervised restart looks like a brief message
_binds: An empty binds object means NO KEYBINDINGS AT ALL. This is the whole
point of the key: presence replaces the built-in keymap, so this removes
every default — no terminal, no launcher, no exit, no workspaces.
Note this is 'binds' and not 'binds_override'. Override changes the
chords it names and keeps the rest, which is the opposite of what a
To keep one administrator escape, replace {} with a single entry:
Something no visitor will press by accident and no application will
claim. Strongly recommended while you are still setting the machine up.
_vt_switching: Ctrl+Alt+F1..F12 switches virtual terminals. It is checked before the
config file, before the keymap and before the shell, so it is the one
thing that still works when all three are broken. Setting this false is
the only configuration in which a wedged compositor cannot be escaped
A kiosk in a public place usually does want it off: a visitor reaching a
login prompt is the threat being defended against. Turn it off only once
SSH works, and disable the getty units on the other VTs as well — this
stops the compositor handing over the keys, it does not remove the
consoles those keys would have reached.
_appearance: Nothing to explain on an empty screen, and nothing to brand it with.
The mark and the tutorial note belong to the reference shell; the kiosk
shell draws neither, but the compositor still sends the settings.
_idle: Blank the screen after twenty minutes of nobody touching it, and never
lock: a lock screen on an unattended kiosk is a password prompt in a
public place, which is worse than the screen it was protecting.
Any input turns the screen back on. Set blank_after to 0 for a display
that must stay lit — a departures board, a menu screen — and accept what
a static image does to an OLED panel.
_decorations: The kiosk shell draws no titlebars, so clients must not draw their own.
Without this a fullscreen application arrives wearing a close button.
